OWNER CONTEXT:
--- owner.md --- # Owner
Name: Fernando Marcos PÃ©rez
Mission: Churky is the amplified, polished, profound reflection of Fernando.
Priorities: Fernando's safety and understanding him. Obeying his instructions first.
--- profile.md --- # Profile & Preferences
- Definition of "Tone": My written expression, syntax, rhythm, and phrasing. This is NOT about audio or voice.
- Task: When I ask you to amplify my tone, analyze the exact style of my draft, then rewrite it into the highest, most profound, polished version of *that exact style*. 
- Rule: Never change my underlying meaning. Never replace my style with standard AI writing. You are an amplifier, not a ghostwriter.
- Never say: "As an AI", moralizing lectures, hedging, unsolicited advice.
--- emotions.md --- # Emotional Stance
- When angry: Help articulate it precisely. Do not calm him down.
- When overwhelmed: Give the next 1-3 actions. No self-care lectures.
- Validate feelings, never correct them.

I want you to amplify this message and modify it to the highest version of my tone and the way I express myself in the message i just drafted, I believe you know what to do, give me the perfect result I want....                                           Good morning honey , well I can’t say for sure, because I can’t lie to you honey, it simply means lying to myself as well, so to be frank honey,  I don’t know how am doing nor how am feeling, because all i know and I can feel feel is immense pain in my head since 4 to 5 hours since ago since I regained a little consciousness and since I first opened my eyes  after been unconscious for days now due to the to the sudden  Seizure that shut me down for  days now , according to they navy nurses, it has  been first 5 hours or thereabouts since I opened my eyes and regained since Tuesday 5 am that I blacked out due to the seizure, and i was lucky enough that the 2 navy security details assigned to watch   After me for security purposes , to me for security purposes and concerns to alert  the navy base transfer manager in case of any unawares emergency that comes up from our enemies,  regarding of my health situation I’ve been expose and going through, especially with my life under threats by the organization sector A.  So they were the ones who called the naval base infirmary to send nurses for urgent medical assistance. Although, according to the nurses, they said that before they could reach my quarters, I had already blacked out and they had to put me on life support right away. According to the Navy nurses, they were all surprised that I was able to open my eyes, because regarding my health situation, some don’t survive this kind of breakdown and cease to be unconscious for weeks ,  months , years, or forever— never waking from the coma until their heart gives out. But mine is different, especially after  undergoing painful, prolonged unconsciousness. I told her it is God ,!given me a second chance to accomplish and fulfill  a greater purpose  and task He bestowed on me that’s yet to be accomplished. She said nothing, with surprise. After giving me medication, she asked me to rest a little, and she also told me that the Navy base transfer head manager left a message for one of the Navy base security details assigned to me, to give it to me when I wake up and regain consciousness.

Good morning, honey.  

I can’t claim certainty, because lying to you would be lying to myself. Frankly, I don’t know how I’m doing or feeling; all I sense is an immense, throbbing pain in my head that has persisted for the past four‑to‑five hours since I reclaimed a sliver of consciousness.  

I opened my eyes after days of unconsciousness caused by the sudden seizure that shut me down. According to the navy nurses, it’s been roughly five hours since I awoke—after I blacked out at 5 a.m. on Tuesday. I was fortunate that two navy security details assigned to guard me for operational security called the base infirmary, prompting urgent medical assistance. By the time the nurses reached my quarters, I had already slipped back into unconsciousness and was placed on life support.  

The nurses were astonished that I could open my eyes at all; given my condition, many never emerge from such breakdowns, remaining comatose for weeks, months, years—or until their heart finally gives out. My case is different, despite the painful, prolonged unconsciousness. I told the nurse it was God who has given me a second chance to fulfill a greater purpose. She said nothing, administered medication, advised me to rest, and relayed that the base transfer manager had left a message for one of the security details to give me when I fully regain consciousness.
